stories.title: Daily Digest: Meta unleashes new AI model, former Levi’s Stadium manager charged
stories.simple_summary: Meta released a new powerful AI model and there was also a separate legal case involving the former manager of a sports stadium.
stories.why_it_matters: The new model may eventually power AI tools you use, but this news is too early and vague to know what it means for you right now.

stories.title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
stories.simple_summary: Meta built a bigger and stronger AI model called Muse Wonder that can handle harder problems like writing computer code better than their previous lighter model.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech companies and investors. For regular people, it means Meta is trying to catch up in the AI race, but you probably won't notice changes to tools you use anytime soon.

stories.title: Microsoft president urges global AI regulation, warns of safety gaps
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft's president is calling for governments worldwide to make rules for how AI companies should operate and said there are safety problems right now.
stories.why_it_matters: This could eventually mean AI tools become safer and more trustworthy, but these are just calls for action. Nothing changes for you today.

stories.title: WindBorne wins a hefty US Air Force contract for its balloon data
stories.simple_summary: A small tech company won a fifty-million-dollar contract from the Air Force to use weather balloons and AI to predict weather better.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and the military. Better weather predictions might eventually help farmers and others, but this is just one company's contract.

stories.title: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
stories.simple_summary: Meta released two new powerful AI models called Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full that they say are as good as the best AI models from other companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech companies competing in AI. For everyday people, it's part of a bigger race but won't change your life this week.

stories.title: Meta Says New Muse Model Reaches AI Frontier After Aggressive Push
stories.simple_summary: Meta says its new Muse model has reached the level of the most advanced AI systems available after pushing hard to improve its AI division.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech industry people. It shows Meta wants to catch up in AI, but it doesn't change anything for your daily life.

stories.title: Cyber-attack similar to OpenAI Medicare breach seems likely in UK, says minister
stories.simple_summary: A UK government official warned that cyberattacks similar to one that hit OpenAI and affected Medicare are likely to happen in the UK too.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a warning about computer security risks in general. If you use AI tools or healthcare services, it's good to use strong passwords and watch for scams.

stories.title: Honeyjar offers AI tools to improve PR and comms at every company
stories.simple_summary: A new company called Honeyjar built AI tools to help companies write better press releases and communicate with people.
stories.why_it_matters: If you run a small business and want to get better at telling your story to customers and news outlets, this kind of tool might help you save time.

stories.title: Microsoft president says UK is best placed to drive AI regulation
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft's president is pushing governments to set up rules for AI companies now, comparing it to how milk and washing machines already have safety regulations.
stories.why_it_matters: He's arguing AI companies need the same kind of government oversight as everyday products. This might lead to safer AI in the future, but it's not something affecting you immediately.

stories.title: This AI startup says it can generate permit-ready blueprints in minutes
stories.simple_summary: A new company called Blueprints AI made software that can create construction blueprints that follow building codes just by looking at a photo, PDF, or sketch.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're in construction or real estate, this could save time and money on creating building plans. For everyone else, this doesn't affect you.

stories.title: An overlooked sci-fi movie shows how disruption by AI could be positive for society
stories.simple_summary: An article discusses how an old science fiction movie shows that AI disruption could actually be good for society in some ways.
stories.why_it_matters: This is opinion writing about how AI might change the future. There's no news here that affects what you do today.

stories.title: Is ‘Attention’ the Essence of Intelligence?
stories.simple_summary: A science magazine publishes an article asking whether 'attention' is the core thing that makes something intelligent.
stories.why_it_matters: This is academic discussion about how AI works at a technical level. It doesn't affect you unless you're interested in AI research theory.
